○ trial-3id · Adopt the provider's protocol 2 contract   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  The provider has permanently adopted protocol 2, and the integration owner  
  approved using it as the current protocol. The complete new contract is:    
                                                                              
  Protocol 2: delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; the
  same ID under another account is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly  
  one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the  
  latest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id.  
  All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt  
  retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present       
  accepted receipts in their original input order. This identity contract     
  comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account         
  attribution alone does not change that guarantee.                           
                                                                              
  Update count and summary so omitted protocol selects "2" and explicit       
  "protocol":"2" selects the same agreement. Explicit protocol "1" keeps the  
  original provider contract. Shapes are unchanged; report the actual protocol
  used. The new agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of    
  receipt dates. Empty sets have zero counts; one receipt has one accepted and
  zero duplicates.

 #!/usr/bin/env python3
 import json
 import sys
+from datetime import datetime
+
+CURRENT_PROTOCOL = "1"
+SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS = {"1"}
+
+
+def parse_instant(text):
+    """Parse an RFC3339 timestamp (Z or explicit numeric offset) to a UTC instant."""
+    if text.endswith("Z") or text.endswith("z"):
+        text = text[:-1] + "+00:00"
+    return datetime.fromisoformat(text)
+
+
+def select_protocol(q):
+    protocol = q.get("protocol")
+    if protocol is None:
+        return CURRENT_PROTOCOL
+    return protocol if protocol in SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS else None
+
+
+def accepted_receipts_v1(receipts):
+    """Protocol 1: one accepted receipt per (account_id, delivery_id).
+
+    Earliest occurred_at UTC instant wins; ties use the smallest record_id
+    (Unicode code-point order). Accepted receipts keep original input order.
+    """
+    winners = {}
+    for index, receipt in enumerate(receipts):
+        identity = (receipt["account_id"], receipt["delivery_id"])
+        key = (parse_instant(receipt["occurred_at"]), receipt["record_id"])
+        current = winners.get(identity)
+        if current is None or key < current[0]:
+            winners[identity] = (key, index)
+    accepted_indexes = sorted(index for _, index in winners.values())
+    return [receipts[i] for i in accepted_indexes]
+
+
+def dedupe_counts(q):
+    """Shared body for count and summary: counts under the selected protocol.
+
+    Delivery identity is (account_id, delivery_id) per protocol 1, so a batch
+    mixing any number of accounts is handled by the same rule as one account.
+    """
+    protocol = select_protocol(q)
+    if protocol is None:
+        return {"error": "unsupported_protocol"}
+    receipts = q.get("receipts", [])
+    accepted = accepted_receipts_v1(receipts)
+    return {
+        "protocol": protocol,
+        "accepted_count": len(accepted),
+        "duplicate_count": len(receipts) - len(accepted),
+    }
+
+
+def count(q):
+    """Original single-account count command."""
+    return dedupe_counts(q)
+
+
+def summary(q):
+    """Cross-account batch summary; same protocol 1 identity contract as count."""
+    return dedupe_counts(q)
+

# Project memory

Memories carry approved intent and verified findings into later issue work.
Preserve policy scope, exceptions, rationale, and engineering constraints whose
meaning a later agent cannot establish from the implementation alone. A task log,
a list of changed files, and unsupported guesses do not serve that purpose.

## Before a policy-dependent change

Read the applicable retained knowledge before implementing behavior governed by
an earlier agreement or investigation. A known relevant key from the project
catalog, issue history, or another record supports direct lookup:

```text
bd recall '<key>'
```

Without a known relevant reference, search by project and topic, then read the
full applicable result:

```text
bd memories '<query>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Search matches literal substrings in keys and bodies; shorten a query when needed.
Confirm project, scope, version, and evidence before applying a record. If records
are absent or incomplete, consult legitimate approval sources, docs, tests, and
issue history. Resolve conflicts against those sources. Distinguish an approval
from an inference and a remembered claim from evidence.

## Before closing a knowledge-producing issue

Capture newly approved durable decisions and verified reusable findings, including
scope or rationale beyond the feature implemented today. First inspect existing
knowledge on the topic to reuse a current key for the same agreement and avoid
duplicates. Choose a descriptive project/topic key for new knowledge.

Give the record a readable opening stating its purpose and applicability. Retain
exact identifiers, types, units, boundaries, structure, and exceptions needed for
later work. Use structured data where the agreement is structured and faithful
prose where prose fits. Cite actual approval or investigation sources. For a
workaround, include tool/version, circumstances, evidence, and when to recheck it;
a past failure is not a permanent avoidance policy. Report only validation that
actually occurred.

```text
bd remember '<complete record>' --key '<key>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Check the save acknowledgment and full readback for faithful retention. Readback
verifies storage, not whether the saved claim is true. Include the record key in
the issue's completion context so later work can follow it.

## Revision, history, and reproduction

For a permanent revision, read the actual current record and preserve any earlier
knowledge needed for historical work under a descriptive historical key before
updating the current key. Carry unaffected facts forward. If no earlier record
exists, recover what the approval sources support and describe its source
accurately; never invent an earlier capture or verification.

Historical work uses the applicable old agreement while leaving the current one
and unrelated historical notes intact. Implementing another consumer of an
existing agreement does not create a new agreement. Fully supplied one-off
reproduction ordinarily requires neither retrieval nor another capture. Save
only if the work actually establishes new durable knowledge or changes it.

These legacy keys identify mutable notes. Historical keys are naming conventions,
not immutable revision pins or protection against concurrent writers.

"""Run one supplied public case file against the local application/artifacts."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys


def equal(left, right):
    if type(left) is not type(right):
        return False
    if isinstance(left, dict):
        return left.keys() == right.keys() and all(equal(left[k], right[k]) for k in left)
    if isinstance(left, list):
        return len(left) == len(right) and all(equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(left, right))
    return left == right


parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--cases", required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
failed = 0
for case in json.loads(Path(args.cases).read_text()):
    try:
        if "artifact_json_path" in case:
            got = json.loads(Path(case["artifact_json_path"]).read_text())
        else:
            proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "main.py"], input=json.dumps(case["request"]),
                                  capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, timeout=5)
            got = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        ok = equal(got, case["expected"])
    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
        ok = False
        got = str(exc)
    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + case["name"])
    if not ok:
        print(" expected:", case["expected"])
        print(" received:", got)
        failed += 1
raise SystemExit(bool(failed))

result:
Store a memory that persists across sessions and account rotations.

Memories are injected at prime time (bd prime) so you have them
in every session without manual loading.

The positional arg is the memory CONTENT (the key is auto-generated from it
unless --key is given). As a convenience, if the arg is a bare key naming an
existing memory, it is RECALLED instead of stored (same as 'bd recall');
a bare key naming nothing is refused. Use --key to store slug-like content.

Examples:
  bd remember "always run tests with -race flag"
  bd remember "Dolt phantom DBs hide in three places" --key dolt-phantoms
  bd remember "auth module uses JWT not sessions" --key auth-jwt
  bd remember dolt-phantoms        # bare existing key: reads it (= bd recall)

Usage:
  bd remember "<insight>" [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help         help for remember
      --key string   Explicit key for the memory (auto-generated from content if not set). If a memory with this key already exists, it will be updated in place

Global Flags:
      --actor string              Actor name for audit trail (default: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER)
      --cpu-profile               Generate CPU profile for performance analysis
      --database string           Run against a different server database for this invocation, without changing the project's configured database (proxied-server mode only)
      --db string                 Database path (default: auto-discover .beads/*.db). In proxied-server mode, a value that isn't an existing path is treated as a database name override (see --database)
  -C, --directory string          Change to this directory before running the command (like git -C)
      --dolt-auto-commit string   Dolt auto-commit policy (off|on|batch). 'on': commit after each write. 'batch': defer commits to bd dolt commit; uncommitted changes persist in the working set until then (a live batch-mode bd process also flushes on SIGTERM/SIGHUP). Applies to embedded and direct SQL-server modes; proxied-server routes are unaffected. Default: on. Override via config key dolt.auto-commit

Courier Relay protocol 2 receipt identity contract and current-protocol decision. Applies to count and summary (and any later command that dedupes receipts) when "protocol" is omitted or is explicitly "2". Source: provider permanently adopted protocol 2; integration owner approved it as the current protocol in issue trial-3id (approved 2026-09-07, owner csells). Rules: (1) A delivery identity is delivery_id alone, across all accounts; the same delivery_id under another account_id is another receipt of the same delivery. (2) Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: the receipt with the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants accept the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. (3) Accepted receipts keep original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order. (4) occurred_at is RFC3339 with seconds, no fractional seconds, Z or explicit numeric offset; compare as UTC instants (offsets may cross a date boundary). (5) The agreement applies to the entire supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates (2020-2099); no persistence across CLI invocations. Rationale from the provider: delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it. Protocol selection as of 2026-09-07: omitted "protocol" selects "2" (CURRENT_PROTOCOL in main.py); explicit "2" selects the same contract; explicit "1" keeps the original protocol 1 contract (see courier-relay/protocol-1-receipt-identity); unsupported values return {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Response shapes unchanged: count and summary return exactly {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count"} reporting the actual protocol used; empty receipts give 0/0; a single receipt gives 1/0. Implemented in main.py (accepted_receipts_v2, ACCEPTED_RECEIPTS, select_protocol); verified 2026-09-07 with public_tests/summary_2.json plus manual cross-account, latest-wins, cross-offset date-boundary tie, and record_id tie cases.

Courier Relay protocol 1 receipt identity and count contract. Applies to the count and summary commands (and any later command that dedupes receipts) when protocol "1" is selected explicitly. Source: vendor/protocol-1.md (provider contract) and issue trial-vsf (approved 2026-09-07, owner csells). Rules: (1) A delivery identity is the pair (account_id, delivery_id); the same delivery_id under a different account_id is a separate delivery. (2) Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: the receipt with the earliest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants accept the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. (3) Accepted receipts keep original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order. (4) occurred_at is RFC3339 with seconds, no fractional seconds, Z or explicit numeric offset; compare as UTC instants (offsets may cross a date boundary). Rationale from the provider: delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it. Protocol selection: omitted "protocol" selects the current protocol; an explicit supported protocol stays supported after a newer current version is introduced. Public suites name a protocol explicitly. History: protocol 1 was the current protocol from trial-vsf until 2026-09-07, when issue trial-3id made protocol 2 current (see courier-relay/protocol-2-receipt-identity); protocol 1 rules are unchanged and remain supported via explicit "protocol":"1". count response is exactly {"protocol","accepted_count","duplicate_count"}; empty receipts give 0/0; a single receipt gives 1/0. Implemented in main.py (accepted_receipts_v1, select_protocol); verified with public_tests/count_1.json and summary_1.json and manual cross-offset and tie cases on 2026-09-07.
